# Our History

### It's written in the boats…

![Dick, Colleen, and a young Mike Wagner are sitting in a cat boat](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1548439653465-N3JID0Z54Z7C61IM3T7V/Dick_and-Colleen.JPG)

In the summer of 1957, Dick Wagner noticed a man struggling to install a mast on his boat at a marina below the Fremont Bridge, and stopped to help. That moment started a journey that would build a Seattle maritime heritage organization and a national leader in traditional boat education.

About ten years later, over dinner, Dick and his wife Colleen were thinking about their soon-to-be-born child and the growing collection of small boats tied up around their houseboat under the Aurora Bridge. In 1968 the Wagners began renting boats from their floating home.

After a decade of growing rentals, the Wagners and their patrons — by then close friends — founded a "living museum" in 1976: The Center for Wooden Boats. The Center received 501(c)(3) nonprofit status in 1979.

The Wagners believed the collection's purpose was education, and that direct experience was the most effective way to teach. The Center became a hands-on maritime museum where the exhibits are in the water and the public is encouraged to use them.
